ref: All rules (task due_to, three probable rules, possible AAA rule, priority evaluation)
text: Everything is anchored on (clinical_finding "Peripheral vascular disease" "disorder"). On a chronic-condition page the patient's PVD is most naturally recorded as an active condition, and the briefing's own convention for known chronic conditions in a due_to is (active_condition X). If the system records PVD as an active condition rather than a clinical finding, none of these rules fire. The builders' choice keeps the test's check_for constraint satisfied, but it should be confirmed that a recorded PVD condition matches the clinical_finding form, or the priority/diagnosis due_tos should accept either form.

ref: Check for urgent peripheral vascular disease conditions
text: The check_for asks for 'Pain in lower limb' twice: once with Sudden onset + Severe + At rest (acute rule) and once with At rest only (critical rule). Because evidence matches by exact string, a nurse who records the sudden severe at-rest form will trigger the acute rule but not the critical one unless the plain at-rest form is also recorded; in practice the acute path is the more urgent so nothing is lost, but the duplicate prompt is a nuisance and the page treats 'leg pain at rest' as one question.

No possible-PVD pre-screen rule from intermittent claudication (page's first bullet), so the file cannot be reached from a presenting complaint; it only runs once PVD is already recorded. Acceptable for a chronic-condition page, noted for completeness.

text: Not in red box; encodes outside element p154-a24fed8b (pulsatile mass: refer for possible AAA) as possible. Good, but outside element is a management referral so this is optional; the rule is also redundant with the probable rupture rule only in part.
Page's urgency for CLI is 'discuss same-day urgency with specialist', arguably less than Urgent; Urgent for all three is a judgement call the page does not clearly justify.

Every rule (check task, three probable rules, possible AAA, priority) is anchored on (clinical_finding Peripheral vascular disease). PVD is not a common symptom or warning sign, so a patient presenting with sudden painful pale leg or pulsatile abdominal mass with back pain but no previously recorded PVD will not trigger any of this logic. This follows the page wording ('patient with PVD and any of') but limits reach, especially for ALI and rAAA which are emergencies.

ref: Diagnose probable critical limb ischaemia in peripheral vascular disease
text: Rest pain is encoded as (Pain in lower limb + At rest qualifier) while ALI uses (Pain in lower limb + Sudden onset + Severe + At rest). Evidence matching is by exact s-expression; unless qualifier subsumption is applied, a patient recorded with the ALI pain form would not also satisfy the CLI rest-pain criterion. Harmless clinically (ALI is also Urgent) but worth noting.

ref: Diagnose probable ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm in peripheral vascular disease
text: 'BP < 90/60' encoded as SBP<90 OR DBP<60, so a DBP of 58 with SBP 120 plus pulsatile mass yields probable rupture. Consistent with the gold standard convention; flagged only for awareness.
